AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To evaluate local anesthetic infiltration with 0.5% bupivacaine in the management of surgical wound pain during the postoperative period.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: A randomized controlled trial was carried out from 1 January to 1 June 2017 SCOPE: Cardiovascular Surgery Department and Heart Area.

AbstractText.Label: PATIENTS
AbstractText.content: Patients scheduled for implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) placement, aged ≥ 18 years and who following verbal and written explanation of the purpose of the study, accepted and signed the informed consent document. The total sample consisted of 82 patients divided into anesthetic infiltration group (n=39) and control group (n=43).

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTIONS
AbstractText.content: Patients were randomized to the control group (conventional management) or anesthetic infiltration group (infiltration of 0.5% bupivacaine at surgical wound closure after ICD implantation). Pain intensity was rated with the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) during the postoperative period at rest and in the course of movement.

AbstractText.Label: VARIABLES OF INTEREST
AbstractText.content: Patient gender, sex and age, type and time of surgery, intensity of pain, surgical wound complications and rescue analgesia.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The control group showed the greatest pain during the postoperative period according to the NRS resting score (at 2hours NRS=6.3; P=.001, 4hours NRS=6.1; P=.002 and 12hours NRS=4.1; P=.004) and in the course of movement (at 2hours NRS=7.1; P=.001, 4hours NRS=6.9; P=.003 and 12hours NRS=5.1; P=.005).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: The infiltration of 0.5% bupivacaine in the surgical incision after ICD implantation reduces patient pain at rest and in the course of movement during the postoperative period.
